# Assembly guide: Spaceship (FocusPod v2), 2 people, a 5 mm hex drive

| Doc code | Part number | Revision | Status | Date | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V2-INS-001 | 100000 POD · Pod hoàn chỉnh | P04 | DRAFT | 2026-10-31 | Packing and Assembly Engineer |

Revision P04 is the pod's own revision: this guide is built on skeleton P04, and the files of part 100000 share one revision (conventions §7 and §8). This is the guide's first issue. It follows the general assembly and the subassembly drawings when they exist and doesn't replace them (guideline §5.1). Labels like **1-05** are the packing labels of [`910000_P01_PACKAGING-PLAN_PKG.md`](../../07-Packaging/910000_P01_PACKAGING-PLAN_PKG.md); every number carries a status (conventions §9).

## Result

1. **Two people, a cordless driver with a 5 mm hex bit and the kit's 5 mm key, 22 steps: about 113 minutes (3.8 person-hours)** on the layout study's unit times and the PM's rulings of 2026-11-01. That is inside REQ-ASM-01's 4-hour limit; the PM's target for v2 is about 104 minutes (REQ-ASM-01 asks about 1 hour). The timed trial on the prototype decides, and section 6 shows where the time goes.
2. **92 bolts of the joints register, each captive in its part but the roof grille's 4, which come in a bag with the grille (J-AIR-03): 80 × 838001 (M6 × 16) and 12 × 838002 (M6 × 25) pins and lock screws**, each with its 838004 washer already on. They match the register joint by joint (section 5). Every site fixing is in the register now: the corner keys hook in and DL and DR stand on spigots, with no site bolts (J-BASE-02, J-FRONT-02); the door hinges and the air parts' fixings in DR stay on hold there.
3. **Every part weighs 20 kg or less except the glass** (D-03). The door unit (48.6 kg) and the fixed glass (28.7 kg) are carried by both people with 2 suction lifters.
4. **Order rules:** all walls before the front; the ceiling closes by order (its side walls' top corner bolts stay finger-tight until both halves are in, R-J9); the door hangs before DT (PM ruling); DR's bolts are driven before the air column stands (J-FRONT-01); every bolt before the linings that cover its bay.
5. **Pictures:** each step that fits parts has a line drawing made from the parts' own CAD on main, outside Fusion, with the drawing generator's exact hidden-line projection: the step's parts black, each with its packing label, and the parts fitted before grey. A part that goes into another is drawn clear of it, with an arrow into place, and an arrow shows any move whose direction matters. A part whose CAD is still to come is drawn dashed from the skeleton's block and marked CAD TO COME. The four renders below show the whole pod.

## 1. Before you start

- **The crew.** Person A leads the lifting and holds each part in place; Person B drives the bolts from inside. Both lift the glass, the long parts and anything overhead.
- **Tools.** The kit supplies one tool, the 5 mm ball-end hex key 108001, in the OPEN FIRST kit (109000, label 2-21): for the roof grille's 4 bolts, the final check and as a backup (REQ-ASM-03). The installers bring a cordless driver with a 5 mm hex bit long enough to reach through the 19 mm access holes, its clutch set to the joints register's value; the bolt times assume it (the PM's ruling, 2026-11-01).
- **Handling aids** (not tools: ISS-047, ISS-064): 2 suction lifters (two-cup, each rated 40 kg or more; assumption), 2 step stools with 2 treads, a 600 mm spirit level, a utility knife for straps and film, cut-resistant gloves and safety shoes.
- **The room:** see the [install sheet](100000_P04_POD-INSTALL-SHEET_INS.md): at least 2550 mm clear height, a floor flat within the glides' range, a door at least 810 mm wide (REQ-ASM-06), room round the 2500 × 1700 footprint to lay the parts out, and a 120 V, 60 Hz wall outlet (NEMA 5-15, 15 A) within reach of the pod's cord (D-133).
- **Directions:** left and right as seen from outside, facing the door (conventions §4). Position codes: walls L1 and L2 (left, lower and upper), R1 and R2 (right), B1 to B4 (back: lower left, lower right, upper left, upper right); ceiling C1 (left) and C2 (right); decor blocks DL, DR, DT.
- **The clock** (REQ-ASM-01; its start and stop are PROPOSED): it starts with the pallets unwrapped on site and stops with the pod closed, powered and the fans running, after the final check (step 21). Step 22 fits the ledge after the clock.

## 2. Safety

- **Glass.** The door unit is 48.6 kg and the fixed glass 28.7 kg: always both people and both suction lifters. Check each lifter's vacuum before every lift. Get each pane upright by tilting it up in the crate on its padded long edge, both lifters at its top edge, onto the padded glass rest; never lift a pane flat and never turn it on a corner. Carry glass upright, never flat and never over anyone. Set it down only on the padded glass rests or in its channel, never on a corner or a hard floor. Leave the protective film on. The glass stays in its crate until its step.
- **Weight.** Every other part is 20 kg or less (D-03); parts longer than 1.6 m or heavier than 15 kg are carried by both people.
- **Height.** Never two people on one step stool. The ceiling halves, the soffit, its cartridge, DT and the ceiling linings are lifted by both people, each on a stool of their own, onto a rest, and let go before anyone fixes them: no one holds a part overhead to fix it (the PM's ruling, 2026-11-01). For the other high work, one works from a stool and the other hands up.
- **Hands.** Keep fingers off the joint faces while a panel is lowered onto its spigots and while a bolt pulls a seam shut.
- **Bolts.** The cordless driver, its clutch set to the joints register's value (the Joints Engineer's, with margin against the rivnut spinning out; the torque is on HOLD until the rivnut test T06, HOLD-01, D-48): drive until the seam closes onto its stop and the clutch slips. No impact drivers, no extension bars.
- **Electrics.** Power stays off until step 20, when the pod's cord goes into the room's 120 V wall outlet (D-133). The mains side comes wired from the factory on its tested plug-in harness (D-87): nothing is wired on site, and everything inside runs on 12 V (D-10).
- **Packaging.** Hold a strap while cutting it. Keep film and foam off the walking area.

## 3. How the joints work (read once)

- **Captive bolts.** Each bolt sits in the edge tube of the part placed second, with its washer, pulled back and held by a grommet (joints register 2.2). You only turn it: the driver's 5 mm bit (or the kit's key) goes through the Ø19 hole from the 60 × 60 fill pocket in that panel's bay. The one exception is the roof grille: its 4 bolts go in from the roof with their washers (step 17, J-AIR-03).
- **Spigots.** Every wall and ceiling part stands on two Ø8 spigots, a round hole at one end and a slot at the other, before its first bolt (REQ-ASM-04). If a part doesn't drop on, lift it and seat it again; never force it.
- **Two bolts, one key.** 838001 (M6 × 16) for the 80 other bolts: each pulls its joint onto its 2.26 mm metal stop or its seat. 838002 (M6 × 25) pins at the 10 closing-seam positions (B1–B2, B3–B4, C1–C2): snug only, they hold the faces level and pull nothing (joints register 2.10). Two more lock the soffit on its hanger studs (J-AIR-01).
- **Order of tightening** (joints register 2.7, R-J9): closing-seam pins first, then the stopped seams; the side walls' top corner bolts and the ceiling's side bolts last, once both ceiling halves are in.
- **Linings last.** Every bolt is driven through a bay that a lining cassette covers later, so check each wall's bolts before its cassette goes on.

## 4. Steps

### Step 1. Unpack and set the parts down at their places

- **Time:** about 12 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-21** POD - INSTALLATION KIT (OPEN FIRST) (3.5 kg).
- **Fasteners:** none.
- **Person A:** Cuts the straps and film on pallet 2 and hands the tiers down, top first: the OPEN FIRST kit and the ceiling cassettes, then tiers 4 to 2. Leaves the glass crate closed on the pallet.
- **Person B:** Sets every part from pallet 2 down at its own place round the pod, as the label map shows, felt and ACP faces up on floor protection, and keeps the seam prop (the 45 × 45 timber labelled SEAM PROP - STEP 7, with its plywood foot and cap, from tier 3) for step 7; opens the kit (hex key, this guide, label map) and ticks the packing list.
- **Check before the next step:** Every label on the packing list is found and lies at its place. Nothing leans on the glass crate. Pallet 1 stays strapped until step 3.

### Step 2. Base band

![Step 2](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-02_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 10 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-04** BASE - BAND ASSY - BACK (3.4 kg), **2-05** BASE - BAND ASSY - SIDE - LH (2.6 kg), **2-06** BASE - BAND ASSY - SIDE - RH (2.6 kg), **2-07** BASE - BAND ASSY - FRONT - FIXED GLASS (2.5 kg), **2-14** BASE - SMALL PARTS CARTON (1.1 kg).
- **Fasteners:** the 6 corner keys hook in, no site bolts (J-BASE-02).
- **Person A:** Sets the left and right side bands on their glides. Then, with B at the other end, lowers the back band straight down between them: the slots in its end caps take both side bands' back-corner studs from below, and it comes to rest on its own glides (D-129). Then the front pieces, each offered 10 mm high, pushed along its studs and lowered onto its glides: FL1, then FL2 at the knee (under DL), then the intake support rail with the mesh intake piece under DR, DR's support and the closing plate, and last FR1, the piece under the fixed glass, onto the rail (J-BASE-02).
- **Person B:** Checks the band with the spirit level, corner to corner, and turns only the glides that are out, from above with the hex key. The glides come preset from the factory (D-87); the glide is HOLD and must take the same 5 mm key (REQ-ASM-03). Then, with A, lays a PE sheet from the packing over the room floor inside the band, clear of the soft lip, for the rest of the work: the room floor is the pod's floor now (D-132).
- **Caution:** Nobody lifts the back band or stands on it until B1 and B2 bolt through its top wall in step 3: until then only its weight holds it on the studs (J-BASE-02).
- **Check before the next step:** Band level within the spirit level's bubble; the back band resting on its glides with both end caps down over the studs; every front piece hooked home; the soft lip on the band's inner face touches the room floor all round (D-132); the mesh piece's support stands; the fixed glass's U-channel, fitted on the sill at the factory, is clean and undamaged.

### Step 3. Lower back wall: B1, B2

![Step 3](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-03_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 2 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **1-01** WALL - PANEL ASSY - BACK LOWER - B1 (8.6 kg), **1-02** WALL - PANEL ASSY - BACK LOWER - B2 (11.5 kg).
- **Fasteners:** 8 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-BASE-01); 3 × 838002 M6 × 25 (J-WALL-03). Tool: the cordless driver with its 5 mm bit; the kit's key as a backup.
- **Person A:** Stands B1 on its band spigots (round hole and slot), skin out, and holds it upright; then B2 the same, against B1. B2 carries the power unit, wired and tested at the factory (11.6 kg).
- **Person B:** From inside, through the fill pockets: first the 3 pins of the B1-B2 closing seam, snug only; then B1's and B2's 4 base bolts each (pins first: joints register 2.7, R-J11).
- **Check before the next step:** Both panels sit down on their stops; the B1-B2 gap looks even top to bottom (5.5 mm nominal).

### Step 4. Lower side walls: L1, R1

![Step 4](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-04_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 3 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **1-03** WALL - PANEL ASSY - SIDE LOWER - LH (11.2 kg), **1-04** WALL - PANEL ASSY - SIDE LOWER - RH (11.2 kg).
- **Fasteners:** 8 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-BASE-01); 6 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-WALL-02). Tool: the cordless driver with its 5 mm bit; the kit's key as a backup.
- **Person A:** Stands L1 on its band spigots about 3.4 mm out from B1's edge, where the seam gasket stands proud (D-167), and holds it; then R1 the same at B2.
- **Person B:** Drives the 4 base bolts of each, then the 3 lower back-corner bolts each side (L1-B1, R1-B2), from the back panels' bays: they pull each side panel in onto its stops, squeezing the gasket (D-167).
- **Check before the next step:** Corners closed onto their stops; side panels' front edges in line with the band's front end.

### Step 5. Upper back wall: B3, B4

![Step 5](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-05_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 2 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **1-05** WALL - PANEL ASSY - BACK UPPER - B3 (8.6 kg), **1-06** WALL - PANEL ASSY - BACK UPPER - B4 (8.6 kg).
- **Fasteners:** 8 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-WALL-01); 3 × 838002 M6 × 25 (J-WALL-03). Tool: the cordless driver with its 5 mm bit; the kit's key as a backup.
- **Person A:** Lifts B3 onto B1's top spigots (step stool), then B4 onto B2's, dropping past the closing seam's lead-in chamfer.
- **Person B:** First the 3 pins of the B3-B4 closing seam, snug only; then the 4 horizontal-seam bolts under each (B1-B3, B2-B4).
- **Check before the next step:** Seams closed; skins flush across the horizontal seam.

### Step 6. Upper side walls: L2, R2

![Step 6](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-06_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 3 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **1-07** WALL - PANEL ASSY - SIDE UPPER - LH (11.3 kg), **1-08** WALL - PANEL ASSY - SIDE UPPER - RH (11.3 kg).
- **Fasteners:** 8 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-WALL-01); 6 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-WALL-02). Tool: the cordless driver with its 5 mm bit; the kit's key as a backup.
- **Person A:** Lifts L2 onto L1's spigots about 3.4 mm out from B3's edge (D-167), then R2 onto R1 the same at B4.
- **Person B:** Drives the 4 horizontal-seam bolts each (L1-L2, R1-R2), then the 3 upper back-corner bolts each side (L2-B3, R2-B4) FINGER-TIGHT only.
- **Check before the next step:** The 6 upper corner bolts are finger-tight, so the wall tops can follow the ceiling (R-J9).

### Step 7. Ceiling: C1, C2

![Step 7](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-07_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 6 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **1-09** CEILING - PANEL ASSY - C1 (10.0 kg), **1-10** CEILING - PANEL ASSY - C2 (10.9 kg).
- **Fasteners:** 4 × 838002 M6 × 25 (J-CEIL-02); 16 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-CEIL-01). Tool: the cordless driver with its 5 mm bit; the kit's key as a backup.
- **Person A:** First stands the seam prop (the timber labelled SEAM PROP, kept from pallet 2's packing in step 1) upright on its plywood foot, on one 5 mm setting packer from the kit, midway between the side walls and in line with their front edges: under the front end of the C1-C2 seam. Its 150 mm cap straddles the seam with about 50 mm to spare either side, so nothing needs measuring, and it stands on its own. With B on a second stool, lifts C1 from inside onto its back spigots (on B3), its side against L2 and its seam corner onto the prop's cap, and both let go: C1 rests on the wall tops and the prop before any bolt (no one holds a part overhead to fix it). Then C2 the same, dropping past C1's lead-in, its seam corner onto the cap beside C1's. C2 carries the roof slot. Each half leans its side wall's top out about 3.4 mm as it goes down (about 24 N, D-167): the upper corner bolts are still finger-tight for this, and the side-edge bolts pull the walls back in. The prop is cut 5 mm short of the corners' 2354 mm, so where the floor is high under it, the packer stays out: the prop can't hold a corner up.
- **Person B:** Drives the 4 pins of the C1-C2 closing seam and, as soon as they are in, takes the seam prop and its packer away; the prop stays with the pod, as taking the ceiling down needs it again. Then the 8 back-edge bolts up from the back panels' top bays, then the 8 side-edge bolts; last, tightens the 6 upper corner bolts left finger-tight in step 6.
- **Caution:** Nobody leans on the seam prop or brushes it while C1 goes up: on its foot alone it tips easily, until C1's corner sits on it.
- **Check before the next step:** Ceiling seams closed; the C1-C2 gap even (4.3 to 6.7 mm); all 6 upper corner bolts now tight.

### Step 8. Left decor block DL

![Step 8](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-08_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 2 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-08** FRONT - DECOR BLOCK ASSY - DL (12.3 kg).
- **Fasteners:** 6 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-FRONT-01); DL locates on its 2 pins in L1's front member, no bolts at the band (D-169). Tool: the cordless driver with its 5 mm bit; the kit's key as a backup.
- **Person A:** With B, carries DL (2.3 m) from its place to the front-left and sets it on the band about 3.4 mm out from L1's and L2's front edges, hinge halves toward the door opening, and holds it there while B bolts it: its 2 pins go into the slots in L1's front member before the seam strip touches (D-169).
- **Person B:** Drives 3 bolts into DL from each of L1's and L2's front bays (6); they pull DL in on its 2 pins onto its stops (D-169). DL has no spigots under it and needs no bolt at the band.
- **Check before the next step:** DL on its stops all along; DL plumb (spirit level on its door-side face); the hinge halves free.

### Step 9. Fixed glass, then the right decor block DR

![Step 9](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-09_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 12 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-01** FRONT - FIXED GLASS UNIT (28.7 kg), **2-03** FRONT - DECOR BLOCK ASSY - DR (18.9 kg).
- **Fasteners:** 6 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-FRONT-01); DR stands on its spigots on its support, no bolts (J-FRONT-02). Tool: the cordless driver with its 5 mm bit; the kit's key as a backup.
- **Person A:** Opens the crate. With B, tilts the fixed glass up on its padded long edge, both suction lifters at its top edge, onto the padded glass rest; then both carry it upright and drop its bottom edge into the U-channel already fitted on the sill, onto its setting blocks. A clamps the 2 glass stays from the kit on its top edge and sets their props on the base band, so the glass stands on its own.
- **Person B:** With A, carries DR (2.3 m, 18 kg) to the right of the opening; both slide it in from the side so its channels take the glass's right and diagonal edges, back onto its stops. Drives 3 bolts into DR from each of R1's and R2's front bays (6); DR stands on its spigots on its support (J-FRONT-02). Only then do the stays come off.
- **Caution:** Nobody carries DR alone and nobody holds the glass by hand while DR comes in: the stays hold the glass, both people carry DR (2.3 m; the 2-person rule).
- **Check before the next step:** Glass seated in all three channels so far, its free edge plumb; DR on its stops; both stays back in the kit. Do this before the air column: DR's right-hand bolts can't be reached once it stands (J-FRONT-01).

### Step 10. Door (before DT)

![Step 10](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-10_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 10 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-02** FRONT - DOOR UNIT (48.6 kg).
- **Fasteners:** the hinge set's own locking parts (FRONT; the hinges are HOLD until a rated set is named); the kick strip's two end brushes, pressed on by hand (368008 at the fixed glass's end, 368009 at DL's end; both HOLD).
- **Person A:** Stacks setting packers from the kit on the room floor where the door's bottom corners land, each stack as high as the base band's bottom edge beside it (about 10 mm; the door's kick strip hangs on that line and the room floor is not flat, D-132). With B, tilts the door unit up in the crate on its padded long edge, both suction lifters at its top edge (each lifts about 12 kg at the start), onto the padded glass rest; then both carry it upright (about 25 kg each) and stand it on the packers, so its hinge halves meet DL's at their height, and lower them on.
- **Person B:** Secures the hinges as the named set requires (HOLD) and slides the packers out. Then fits the kick strip's two end brushes from the door's kit bag (taped to the kick strip), the door held still (see the caution). Each goes on with its 3M VHB LSE tape at 10 °C or warmer, per 3M's own sheet: first wipes the end face with the bag's IPA wipe, then stands the brush on the room floor against it and presses it firmly along its whole length (D-153, D-154). 368008, at the fixed glass's end, goes on with the door only just open, so it meets the floor close to where it seals; 368009, the longer-pile brush at DL's end, with the door wide open, as at the pivot it is out of reach otherwise. Then swings the door slowly to 90 degrees and back, checking that its kick strip runs level with the band's bottom edge, about 10 mm over the room floor, and that the drop seal comes down onto the floor and each brush closes against the end plate beside it when it shuts (D-132, D-150). The hinges hold the door at its closed position; there is no lock (D-83).
- **Caution:** Pinch points: the door hangs on hinges still on HOLD and shuts to 11 mm at the hinge end and 4.5 mm at the latch end. While B works at the kick strip's ends, A holds the door, or a packer wedges its free corner, and fingers stay clear of the hinge side.
- **Check before the next step:** The door hangs before DT goes on: DT's underside is only 4 mm above the door top (PM ruling). Door swings freely, no rub; both end brushes stand on the floor along their whole length.

### Step 11. Top decor block DT, from above

![Step 11](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-11_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 2 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-11** FRONT - DECOR BLOCK ASSY - DT (7.9 kg).
- **Fasteners:** 4 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-FRONT-03). Tool: the cordless driver with its 5 mm bit; the kit's key as a backup.
- **Person A:** First drapes a PE sheet from the packing over DL's top and down its 45 degree slope, where DT's end will bear, and tapes it on DL's top so it can't slide off the slope: the slip sheet that keeps the two skins from scuffing (D-152). From a step stool outside the front, with B on a second stool, lowers DT from above onto DL and DR so its slot takes the glass's top edge, and both let go: DT rests on DL's slope and DR before its bolts.
- **Person B:** Drives DT's 4 bolts to the ceiling (J-FRONT-03), then takes the tape off DL's top and pulls the slip sheet out from between DT and DL's slope.
- **Check before the next step:** The slip sheet is out; the glass's top edge is in DT's channel; 4 mm head gap over the door all along; the top band line straight; the door's strike 368102 closes onto the 35 N magnetic catch 368007 in DT's underside (D-83).

### Step 12. Electrics, first fix (power off)

- **Time:** about 1 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-12** ELECTRICAL - KIT - HARNESS, CORD SET, HUB ZONE, LIGHTS (2.4 kg).
- **Fasteners:** none.
- **Person A:** Plugs the factory-tested harness together at each panel seam and runs the plug-in feeds for the light shelf and the hub to their ends (D-87).
- **Person B:** Hands parts from the electrical kit and checks each connector against the wiring diagram (ELECTRICAL design).
- **Check before the next step:** Every seam connector latched before any cassette closes its bay.

### Step 13. Air parts in DR: the intake riser with its supply fan box

![Step 13](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-13_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 4 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-16** AIR - SUPPLY FAN BOX (13.4 kg).
- **Fasteners:** their fixings in DR (AIR and FRONT design, on hold).
- **Person A:** Before the wall linings (DR's inner face can't come off past R1's and R2's cassettes), lifts DR's removable inner face off; with B, slides in the intake riser, its supply fan box (2 fans) joined at its top in the factory, down to its foot over the mesh space (D-87).
- **Person B:** Mates the fan box's plug-in connector; refits the inner face.
- **Check before the next step:** Riser foot sits over the opening; fan box connector latched; inner face back on all round.

### Step 14. Wall linings: 8 cassettes

![Step 14](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-14_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 8 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **1-11** LINING - CASSETTE - SIDE LOWER - RH (10.3 kg), **1-12** LINING - CASSETTE - SIDE UPPER - RH (9.9 kg), **1-13** LINING - CASSETTE - SIDE LOWER - LH (10.3 kg), **1-14** LINING - CASSETTE - SIDE UPPER - LH (9.9 kg), **1-15** LINING - CASSETTE - BACK LOWER - B1 (8.0 kg), **1-16** LINING - CASSETTE - BACK LOWER - B2 (8.0 kg), **1-17** LINING - CASSETTE - BACK UPPER - B3 (8.4 kg), **1-18** LINING - CASSETTE - BACK UPPER - B4 (8.4 kg).
- **Fasteners:** none.
- **Person A:** Fits R1's and R2's cassettes first (the air column needs them), then L1, L2, B1 to B4. Each lower cassette (R1, L1, B1, B2) sits on its ledge, the steel angle along the panel's bottom rail, its bottom return on the ledge's pad, and is pressed onto its clips, which only hold (D-170); each upper cassette stands on the one below through the foam strip in their joint and is pressed onto its clips. DR's inner face is already back on: it can't come off past R1's and R2's cassettes (the PM's ruling).
- **Person B:** Hands each cassette up felt-out and lines it up with the hook-and-loop; checks each clip has locked.
- **Check before the next step:** Every bolt in its bay was driven before the bay is closed. Each cassette touches nothing but its clips and, below it, its ledge's pad or the foam strip on the cassette below (D-170).

### Step 15. Air column and supply cartridge

![Step 15](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-15_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 7 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-10** AIR - AIR COLUMN (8.1 kg), **2-17** AIR - SPLITTER CARTRIDGE - COMMON (10.6 kg).
- **Fasteners:** the column hangs on its 2 factory-set hook studs and stands on 2 spigots, no site bolts (J-AIR-02).
- **Person A:** With B, hangs the air column (2.1 m) on its tool-free hooks in the front-right corner (D-87), its back on DR's inner face and its right side on R1's and R2's linings; lifts its front face off.
- **Person B:** With A, slides the supply cartridge into the column; plugs the hub into the cable chase; A refits the front face.
- **Check before the next step:** Kick grille clear at the floor; the hub zone at about Z 1200 faces the room.

### Step 16. Soffit and exhaust cartridge

![Step 16](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-16_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 5 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-09** AIR - SOFFIT (14.8 kg), **2-18** AIR - SPLITTER CARTRIDGE - COMMON (10.6 kg).
- **Fasteners:** 2 × 838002 M6 × 25 (J-AIR-01). Tool: the cordless driver with its 5 mm bit; the kit's key as a backup.
- **Person A:** With B, both on step stools, lifts the soffit (2.3 m), its exhaust fan box already fitted at the right end (D-87), and hangs it on its 4 hanger studs, set in the ceiling frame at the factory, the fan box under C2's roof slot.
- **Person B:** Drives the soffit's 2 captive lock screws (J-AIR-01); with A, lifts the exhaust cartridge in through the open underside onto its rest in the soffit and lets go (AIR names the rest); plugs the fan box; closes the hinged underside.
- **Check before the next step:** Soffit underside at Z 2120, level; the fan box's top gasket square under the roof slot; the door still clears.

### Step 17. Roof sleeve and grille

![Step 17](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-17_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 3 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** the roof sleeve 611601 and the roof grille 611602 with its 4 bolts and washers in their bag, which came off C2 (1-10) at unpacking.
- **Fasteners:** 4 × 838001 M6 × 16 (J-AIR-03). Tool: the kit's 5 mm key (no room above the roof for the driver).
- **Person A:** From a step stool outside the front right corner, drops the roof sleeve down through C2's roof slot onto the soft gasket on the exhaust fan box's top, its flange on the roof (#263); then lays the roof grille on over it and drives its 4 bolts, each with its washer, into the rivnuts in the sleeve's flange with the 5 mm key, snug (J-AIR-03).
- **Person B:** Inside, opens the soffit's hinged underside and checks from below that the sleeve sits square on its gasket all round; closes the underside.
- **Check before the next step:** Sleeve square on its gasket all round; grille flat on the flange, its 4 bolts snug; no light through the slot with the pod lit.

### Step 18. Ceiling linings: 2 cassettes

![Step 18](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-18_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 5 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-19** LINING - CASSETTE - CEILING - COMMON (9.5 kg), **2-20** LINING - CASSETTE - CEILING - COMMON (9.5 kg).
- **Fasteners:** none.
- **Person A:** With B, lifts each ceiling cassette from below, fill side up, while B hooks its 2 safety catches; both let go and it hangs on its catches. Then both press it up onto its clips behind the soffit.
- **Person B:** Hooks the 2 safety catches of each cassette first, so it hangs on them and no one holds it overhead.
- **Check before the next step:** Both catches on each cassette; front edges 3 mm behind the soffit.

### Step 19. Light shelf

![Step 19](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-19_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 6 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-13** INTERIOR - LIGHT SHELF ASSY (1.6 kg).
- **Fasteners:** the light shelf's fixings (INTERIOR's parts list 810201 names none yet).
- **Person A:** Fits the light shelf along the tops of the side and back walls: the back shelf, the two side shelves, and the down-light channel with its diffuser on the right wall (INTERIOR 810201).
- **Person B:** Plugs the light shelf feed.
- **Check before the next step:** Shelves straight; no cable shows.

### Step 20. Power on and self-test: fans run

- **Time:** about 3 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** none.
- **Fasteners:** none.
- **Person A:** Plugs the pod's cord into the room's 120 V wall outlet (NEMA 5-15, D-133) and switches on.
- **Person B:** Presses the hub's self-test button: both fan pairs, the lights and the sensors run, and it shows pass or fail (D-87). Then checks air out at the kick grille and into the soffit grille, and the CO2 reading.
- **Check before the next step:** Self-test passes and the fans run on both paths. The clock stops after the final check, the next step (REQ-ASM-01: closed, powered, fans running).

### Step 21. Final check and film

- **Time:** about 7 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** none.
- **Fasteners:** none.
- **Person A:** Checks the door: swing to 90 degrees, no rub, closes onto DT's magnetic catch 368007 with the magnetic seal pair meeting on the glass edges (D-83), drop seal down on the room floor when closed (D-132). Then, with the pod lit and the room dark, walks round it: no light at any seam. Ticks the final check list.
- **Person B:** At the same time (the PM's ruling, 2026-11-01), inside first, with the door shut for A's light test: pulls the film off the glass panes' inner faces by their quick-release tabs, lifts the floor sheet and cleans inside. Once A's light test is done, pulls the outside film (the 8 wall skins, the 3 decor blocks, the glass panes' outer faces; 15 panels in all with the inner ones, D-87) and cleans outside.
- **Check before the next step:** Every check in the final check list is ticked.

### Step 22. Work-wall ledge and screen rail, after the clock

![Step 22](img/100000_P04_POD-ASSEMBLY-GUIDE-STEP-22_IMG.png)

- **Time:** about 8 min for 2 people.
- **Parts:** **2-15** INTERIOR - WORK WALL LEDGE ASSY (1.9 kg).
- **Fasteners:** the ledge's 2 brackets 818101 on R1's stiles, on stand-offs through R1's cassette, and the screen rail 818102 on stand-offs to R2's stiles (INTERIOR; both HOLD).
- **Person A:** Holds the 1000 mm ledge on the right (work) wall's lower panel R1, on its 2 brackets.
- **Person B:** Fixes the ledge's brackets to R1's stiles and the screen rail to R2's stiles (INTERIOR 810101 and 818102, D-70).
- **Check before the next step:** Ledge level and firm.

Each step's time is its 2-person work plus half its 1-person work (shared between the two), plus 15% for hand-offs, the layout study's model (`scripts/assembly.py`). Where the time goes:

1. Step 9 (Fixed glass, then the right decor block DR): 12 min.
2. Step 1 (Unpack and set the parts down at their places): 12 min.
3. Step 10 (Door (before DT)): 10 min.
4. Step 2 (Base band): 10 min.
5. Step 14 (Wall linings: 8 cassettes): 8 min.

**The PM's rulings of 2026-11-01 on the next five time sinks cut the clock from 135 minutes to the 113 above:** the installers' cordless driver for the bolts (9.0 min), a rest for each overhead lift so no one holds a part overhead to fix it (6.9 min), and the final check split between the two people (5.8 min); the unit times are assumptions until the timed trial. Lift-off hinges set in the factory (FRONT, in the hinge HOLD's asks, D-138) and a plug-in light shelf (ELECTRICAL's connector choice) would save about 7 minutes more (assumption), to about 106 minutes against the PM's target of about 104. Carrying and unpacking have no cheap fix, and hook-in wall joints, which getting near 1 hour would need, are a redesign the PM ruled out for now.

**D-87 (PM, 2026-10-31) cut the clock from 168 minutes (PR #52) to 127 (PR #59).** The PM took four of the five fixes priced on that model, and they are in the steps now:

| Fix | Steps | Priced on the 168-minute model | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| The exhaust fan box fitted inside the soffit and the intake riser joined to the supply fan box at the factory, plug-in connectors, tool-free hooks for the soffit and the column, one hinged soffit underside | 13, 15 and 16 | 11.4 min (calculation) | AIR (CEILING Engineer), FRONT |
| Glides preset at the factory, corner keys that hook in (12 fewer bolts), band pieces that locate on the keys | 2 | 11.8 min (calculation) | BASE, Joints Engineer |
| The floor foam bonded under the floor panels at the factory (D-132 then removed the floor), and every pallet 2 part set down at its place in step 1 | 1 and every carry | 10.7 min (calculation) | Packing, BASE |
| A factory-tested plug-in harness and a self-test button on the hub | 12 and 20 | 8.1 min (calculation) | ELECTRICAL |

The fifth, moving the film peeling after the clock, was rejected so the number stays honest. Instead the film covers only the 15 faces that show (the 8 wall skins, the 3 decor blocks and both faces of both glass panes; none on the roof skins) and each panel has a quick-release tab. Peeling now takes about 0.9 minutes of the clock, against 3.3 for film on all 17 faces without tabs: 2.4 minutes saved. The layout study's 168 minutes didn't count film at all, so this is time the clock now carries honestly.

The 1-hour target needs more than this: the timed trial showing faster unit times than the layout study assumed, or fewer loose pieces and bolts. The 92 register bolts alone take about 7 minutes of the clock. For scale, hushMeet takes 2 installers 2.5 to 3 hours (source: the market study, as the layout study §4 quotes it).

## 7. Final check list (step 21)

- [ ] Door: swings out to 90 degrees and back with no rub; 4 mm under DT along the head; kick strip level with the band's bottom edge, about 10 mm over the room floor (D-132); closes onto DT's magnetic catch 368007 and stays shut (no lock, D-83); the drop seal comes down onto the room floor when closed; both end brushes stand on the floor along their whole length and close against the end plates beside them.
- [ ] Seals: with the pod lit and the room dark, no light at any seam, at the door's edges or at the fixed glass's edges.
- [ ] Bolts: all 92 register bolts driven, the 10 pins snug, the 6 upper corner bolts tightened after the ceiling; the other fixings of section 5 done.
- [ ] Linings: all 10 cassettes on their clips, both ceiling cassettes on their safety catches, none touching anything but its clips.
- [ ] Air: both fan pairs run; air leaves the kick grille at the column's foot and enters the soffit grille; boost works; the hub shows CO2.
- [ ] Lights: the light shelf works in every scene, including 'call' (D-70).
- [ ] Film peeled from the ACP and the glass; packaging off site, but the seam prop stays with the pod (taking the ceiling down needs it); floor clean.

## 8. Taking it down

Unplug the pod's cord first. Then the reverse order: ledge; ceiling linings (unhook the catches first); soffit underside, exhaust fan box, exhaust cartridge, soffit; air column front face, supply cartridge, air column (it must come out before DR's bolts can be reached, J-FRONT-01); R1's and R2's cassettes off their clips first (DR's inner face can't come off past them, the PM's ruling), then DR's inner face, supply fan box, intake riser; the other wall linings; DT; the door; DR, then the fixed glass with both lifters; DL; the ceiling: first stand the seam prop on its foot under the seam's front end (it holds both corners), then loosen the side walls' top corner bolts, take out the edge bolts and last the 4 seam pins, and lift C2, then C1, off the wall tops and the prop; the upper walls, the lower walls; base band: FR1 off the rail first, then the rail, FL2 and FL1, each lifted 10 mm and drawn back off its studs; the back band lifts straight up out of the side bands' studs once B1 and B2 are off (J-BASE-02). Pack by the labels, into the same places.
